text:
Diego: FYI customer AtlasHealth (INC-573) reports that the quantized endpoint is much slower than fp16 for their workload. They say ~3-4x higher p95. Repro steps incoming.

Sasha: Which quant path are they hitting? int8/4bit/FP8? kernel choice? KV-cache hit rate?

Diego: Endpoint: /v1/engines/redwood-gptx-int8/generate (customer-dedicated-us-west-2)
Logs (sanitised):
```
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] request_id=abc123 model=redwood/gptx-qlora quant_mode=INT8 kernel=matmul_int8_small_seq_v1 seq_len=24 batch=1 kv_cache_hit_rate=0.12 time_total=740ms p95=740ms
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] request_id=abc124 model=redwood/gptx-qlora quant_calibration=running cpu_blocking=120ms
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] request_id=abc125 model=redwood/gptx-qlora fp16 kernel=matmul_fp16_tiled seq_len=24 batch=1 time_total=180ms p95=180ms
```
Repro curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' -d '{"model":"redwood/gptx-qlora","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":64}'`

Priya: Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: 1) kernel selection is preferring an int8 matmul variant that is slower on short sequences (vectorization/tiling mismatch). 2) calibration/quant path is doing a CPU-side requantize/calibration that blocks the request on first few calls — that matches the cpu_blocking=120ms log.

Sasha: Agreed. Also the KV cache hit rate is very low (12%) — that means we lose benefits of cached KV across calls, so per-token matmuls dominate. INT8 kernels can be faster at high throughput and longer seqs, but on seq_len<=32 on A100s some fp16 tiled kernels beat the int8 path.

PerfBot: Profiling summary for request_id=abc123:
- total 740ms
- kernel(matmul_int8_small_seq_v1): 360ms
- requantize_cpu (blocking): 120ms
- kv_cache_miss overhead: 90ms
- batching overhead / dispatch: 50ms
- other: 120ms
(Note: profile sampled over 20 similar requests)

Sasha: Quick mitigation options: 
- Route AtlasHealth to the fp16 model variant or force fp16 kernel via runtime override (fastest short-term).
- Disable in-path calibration for this customer (move to async worker) to remove the 120ms CPU block.
- Increase batching window from 2ms -> 10ms for this pool to help kernel throughput (if customer can accept slight latency tail changes).

Diego: I just pushed a route override to the dedicated pool: `route_override.quant_mode = FP16` for customer-id=atlashealth on pool dedicated-us-west-2-a. Monitoring now.

InfraBot: Route override applied to pool dedicated-us-west-2-a for customer atlashealth at 2026-03-18T14:18:05Z. Canary set to 100% for that customer.

Tom: I'll send customer a quick note: "We've routed you temporarily to FP16 to restore latency while we investigate quant path. Expect update in ~1h. This won't affect your prompt outputs significantly for short prompts." Any objections? :eyes:  

Priya: No objections. For longer term: we're going to change kernel selector heuristics — prefer fp16 kernels for seq_len <= 32 on A100 / T4 families until we improve the int8 small-seq kernel. Also patch the calibration flow to be async and non-blocking (PR in eng-runtime).

Sasha: Action items I can pick up: 
- PR to runtime: prefer_fp16_short_seq heuristic + tests (ETA: today EOD).
- PR to quant pipeline: move calibration to background worker + non-blocking token pipeline (ETA: 2 days).
- Quick benchmark: run matmul_int8_small_seq_v1 vs matmul_fp16_tiled right now on staging A100 with seq=8,16,32 (I'll paste results shortly).

PerfBot: Quick staging microbench (A100, batch=1):
```
seq=8  matmul_int8_small_seq_v1: 1.8 ms  matmul_fp16_tiled: 1.2 ms
seq=16 matmul_int8_small_seq_v1: 3.6 ms  matmul_fp16_tiled: 2.1 ms
seq=32 matmul_int8_small_seq_v1: 7.5 ms  matmul_fp16_tiled: 4.4 ms
```
Numbers confirm fp16 wins at these short seq lengths.

Diego: p95 for the customer after route override: 190ms (down from 740ms). I'll keep this thread updated.

Tom: Customer updated: "Thanks, latency looks much better now. Please keep us posted on the fix to avoid future switches."

Priya: For follow-up: I'll open tracking ticket ENGRT-912 to land selector and async calibration. Sasha — please link your PRs. Diego — ensure we have a fallback policy to auto-route to fp16 if p95 spikes >2x for a customer for >5min.

Sasha: Will do. Adding :thumbsup:.

Diego: Closing the escalated customer impact for now; keeping thread open for the code fixes. If anyone sees regressions in other customers after selector change ping here.

PerfBot: Logged perf regressions and linked ENGRT-912.

InfraBot: Canary metrics for pool dedicated-us-west-2-a: 5m avg p95=195ms, CPU util 47%, KV hit rate 0.13.

Diego: Thanks team — I think we have a good short-term mitigation + path to permanent fix.
